Effective audience: A Customerly support lead who has a draft answer to one frequently asked question.

brief.interpretation: This is a focused activation email for an existing Customerly customer, not an acquisition or sales email. The reader already has one draft FAQ answer; the email should move that answer into their first help-center article and explain that the help center is both customer-searchable and a knowledge source for Aura.
brief.reader:
Selected audience (user-stated constraints): A Customerly support lead who has a draft answer to one frequently asked question..
No further recipient situation is established. Compiled market context is research to check for applicability, not a replacement biography.
brief.reader_segment: SaaS support teams scaling with limited headcount
brief.reader_profile_override: A Customerly support lead who has a draft answer to one frequently asked question.
brief.promise: Turn the drafted FAQ answer into knowledge that customers can search and Aura can learn from.
brief.orientation: Customerly's help center makes support knowledge searchable by customers and available to Aura as an answer source.
brief.arc: In one email, move the reader from holding a standalone draft to seeing it as the ready-made foundation of their first help-center article, then ask them to create that article.
brief.sequence_rationale: A single activation email should begin with the asset the reader already has—the drafted answer—then connect the requested action to its documented operational value: Customerly's help center is searchable by customers and is the same knowledge base Aura learns from. No testimonial, resolution metric, pricing detail, or broader automation pitch is needed to earn this first action. The supplied material does not establish an exact article-creation URL or verified sequence of interface labels, so the CTA should be an unlinked, plain-language in-product instruction and must not invent a navigation path. Can Customerly's help-center article-creation source be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

emails.selection_reason: The reader already possesses the core input—a drafted FAQ answer. Creating one article is the smallest requested activation step, and its value is directly relevant to a support lead because the resulting help-center knowledge can be searched by customers and learned from by Aura.

value_case.reader_benefit: The support lead can turn an answer they have already drafted into reusable support knowledge available through the help center and to Aura.
value_case.mechanism: Customerly provides a help center and AI knowledge base that customers search and Aura learns from; Aura searches articles and uses verified content rather than general AI knowledge.

claim_conditions: The reader has a draft answer to one frequently asked question, as specified by the campaign request.
Do not claim a particular workspace permission, plan entitlement, publishing state, or interface path.
emails.user_request: Write exactly one English activation email from the Customerly team. Reader: A Customerly support lead who has a draft answer to one frequently asked question. Ask them to do one thing: Create the first help-center article. Use a specific, documented first step and explain why it helps this reader. Keep the email under 150 words excluding subject, preview and signature. Avoid unsupported access, plan, timing and outcome claims. Use one CTA with an exact documented destination if available.
emails.job: Get the reader to create their first Customerly help-center article from the FAQ answer they have already drafted.
emails.single_idea: The reader does not need a complete knowledge base to begin: their drafted FAQ answer can become the first article in the help center that customers search and Aura learns from.
emails.felt_need: I already have the answer; I need to make it reusable instead of leaving it as a draft.
emails.status_quo: The frequently asked question and its answer currently remain in a draft rather than as a help-center article.
emails.why_it_fails: While it remains only a draft, it is not part of the documented help center that customers search and Aura learns from.
emails.mechanism: Use the drafted question as the article title and the drafted answer as its starting body, then create it as the first help-center article. Customerly's documented help center is searchable by customers and is the knowledge base Aura learns from; Aura uses verified article content rather than general AI knowledge.
emails.belief_shift: Before: one drafted answer may feel too small to count as a knowledge base. After: it is enough to create the first searchable knowledge source for customers and Aura.
must_not_say: Do not claim that creating the article will reduce tickets, save time, improve resolution rates, or produce any measured outcome.
Do not claim the article will be published, indexed, translated, or used by Aura immediately.
Do not invent menu labels, click sequences, an article editor URL, required permissions, plan access, setup time, or publication timing.
Do not mention pricing, trials, migrations, APIs, live chat, security, customer results, or broad automation metrics.
Do not add a second CTA, including a reply request, documentation link, signup link, demo, or audit.
Do not describe Aura's answers as guaranteed correct merely because she uses verified content.
emails.tone: Warm, direct, and lightly encouraging; treat this as a practical next step, not a sales pitch.
emails.next_step_decision: Complete the first useful help-center setup action by turning the existing FAQ draft into an article.
emails.next_step_value: The action places the drafted answer into the help-center knowledge structure that customers can search and Aura can learn from.
emails.next_step_limit: The supplied evidence does not establish the exact in-app destination, interface labels, publication controls, or when the article becomes available to customers or Aura.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the existing draft feel immediately actionable by connecting it to the reader's first help-center article; avoid metrics, hype, and vague onboarding language.

directions: Write exactly one English activation email.
Ask for one action only: create the first help-center article.
Keep the body under 150 words excluding subject, preview, and signature.
Use the existing draft as the concrete first step and explain its relevance to this support lead.
use: A specific first action grounded in the reader's existing FAQ draft
Aura learning from verified help-center content
avoid: Unsupported access, plan, timing, and outcome claims

brief.voice_notes: Use Customerly's direct, outcome-oriented voice, but keep the register appropriate for customer activation. Short paragraphs are preferable. Refer to Aura by name if needed, without turning the email into an AI automation pitch.
